contacts.name: Kim Bowman
contacts.whyTheyMatter: Kim Bowman founded SCRIN (Southern Community Resilience & Innovation Network), which operates at the exact intersection of rural Southern communities and emerging technology. Her network spans dozens of rural nonprofits and she has direct relationships with community leaders who are already asking for AI literacy resources. A partnership with her could open doors to immediate programming sites and co-grant applications.

outreachMessages.intro:
Hi Kim,

I came across SCRIN's work and was immediately struck by the alignment with what I'm building — the Southern AI Literacy Initiative. We're developing accessible AI education programming specifically for rural Southern communities, and your network represents exactly the kind of grounded, trust-based infrastructure we need to make this real.

I'd love to share what we're working on and explore whether there's a natural fit for collaboration. Would you be open to a brief call?

Warm regards,
[Your Name]
Founder, Southern AI Literacy Initiative
outreachMessages.meetingRequest:
Hi Kim,

Thank you for your time — I'd love to set up a 30-minute call to discuss potential collaboration between SCRIN and the Southern AI Literacy Initiative.

I'm particularly interested in learning more about your community partnerships and exploring how our AI literacy curriculum could complement your existing programs.

I'm flexible on timing — would any of the following work for you?
• [Date/Time Option 1]
• [Date/Time Option 2]
• [Date/Time Option 3]

Looking forward to connecting,
[Your Name]
outreachMessages.followUp:
Hi Kim,

I wanted to follow up on my previous message about the Southern AI Literacy Initiative. I know your schedule is busy, so I'll keep this brief.

We're moving forward with our first pilot programs and I believe SCRIN's community relationships could be genuinely transformative for this work. Even a 20-minute conversation would be valuable.

If now isn't the right time, I completely understand — I'd just appreciate knowing so I can plan accordingly.

Best,
[Your Name]
outreachMessages.partnershipProposal:
Hi Kim,

Following our conversation, I wanted to formally propose a partnership framework between SCRIN and the Southern AI Literacy Initiative.

What I envision: SALI provides curriculum, facilitation training, and technology resources; SCRIN provides community access, trusted relationships, and local context. Together we pursue joint grant funding from sources like the Lumina Foundation and Knight Foundation.

I've drafted a brief MOU outline I'd love to share. Would you be open to reviewing it and scheduling a working session?

Excited about the possibility,
[Your Name]
Founder, Southern AI Literacy Initiative

contacts.name: Dr. James Carter
contacts.whyTheyMatter: Dr. Carter leads technology initiatives at Tuskegee University, one of the most historically significant HBCUs in the country. His position gives him influence over curriculum development, community outreach programs, and external partnerships. Tuskegee's deep roots in rural Alabama and its reputation for practical, community-facing research make it an ideal academic anchor for the Southern AI Literacy Initiative.

outreachMessages.intro:
Dear Dr. Carter,

I'm reaching out because Tuskegee's legacy of applied, community-centered innovation is precisely the kind of institutional DNA the Southern AI Literacy Initiative needs as a partner.

We're building an AI literacy program for rural Southern communities and are looking for an academic anchor that brings both credibility and genuine community trust. Tuskegee University uniquely holds both.

Would you have 30 minutes to discuss potential academic collaboration?

Respectfully,
[Your Name]
Founder, Southern AI Literacy Initiative
outreachMessages.meetingRequest:
Dear Dr. Carter,

I'd like to formally request a meeting to discuss how the Southern AI Literacy Initiative might collaborate with Tuskegee's technology programs.

Specifically, I'm interested in exploring: curriculum co-development, student practicum opportunities, and joint research on AI literacy outcomes in rural communities.

I'm available at your convenience and happy to come to campus.

Best regards,
[Your Name]
outreachMessages.followUp:
Dear Dr. Carter,

I'm following up on my earlier outreach regarding the Southern AI Literacy Initiative. I understand you receive many collaboration requests, and I want to be respectful of your time.

If there's a better person on your team to speak with initially, I'm happy to start there. Or if the timing isn't right, I'd appreciate knowing so I can follow up at a better moment.

Thank you for your consideration,
[Your Name]
outreachMessages.partnershipProposal:
Dear Dr. Carter,

Building on our discussions, I'd like to propose a formal academic partnership between Tuskegee University and the Southern AI Literacy Initiative.

Proposed framework: Tuskegee faculty serve as curriculum advisors and co-investigators on research grants; SALI provides field implementation and community partnerships; both organizations co-author publications on AI literacy outcomes in underserved communities.

This partnership could position Tuskegee as a national leader in community-centered AI education research. I've prepared a brief partnership prospectus — may I share it with you?

With great respect,
[Your Name]
Founder, Southern AI Literacy Initiative

Her endorsement or partnership would significantly strengthen grant applications.

contacts.name: Alabama Rural Electric Cooperative
contacts.whyTheyMatter: Rural electric cooperatives across the South already have deep community trust, existing communication channels into rural homes, and in many cases, broadband infrastructure. The Alabama Rural Electric Cooperative reaches tens of thousands of rural households and has a mandate to serve their communities beyond just electricity. They've funded community programs before and could be both a distribution channel and a funding source.

Given your reach into rural homes across Alabama, I'd love to explore whether there's a partnership opportunity — whether through community programming, co-sponsorship, or other collaboration.

Would someone on your team be available for a brief conversation?

contacts.name: Hope Credit Union
contacts.whyTheyMatter: Hope Credit Union is one of the most respected community development financial institutions (CDFIs) in the Deep South, with a specific mission to serve communities underserved by traditional banking. They have deep relationships with rural Black communities in particular, strong national funding connections, and experience co-funding community education programs. An endorsement from Hope CU carries significant weight with foundations.

Your work in communities that have been systematically excluded from mainstream financial systems is exactly the kind of foundation that the Southern AI Literacy Initiative wants to build on.

We're developing AI literacy programs for rural Southern communities — with a particular focus on economic opportunity and workforce readiness. I believe there's real alignment between our missions.

Congressional staff are often more accessible than their superiors.

contacts.name: Auburn University Extension
contacts.whyTheyMatter: Auburn University's Extension Service has an established presence in every Alabama county, with trusted community educators who already work with rural residents on practical skills. The Extension model — meeting people where they are, focusing on practical application — is exactly right for AI literacy. A partnership with Extension could provide immediate distribution infrastructure and a model for rural reach that would be prohibitively expensive to build from scratch.

outreachMessages.intro:

Auburn Extension's county-by-county presence in Alabama communities represents something that takes decades to build: genuine trust. I'm writing because the Southern AI Literacy Initiative needs exactly that kind of infrastructure.

We're developing accessible AI education for rural Alabama residents — practical content about how AI affects jobs, healthcare decisions, and everyday life. The Extension model of practical, community-based education is the right model for this content.

Would you be open to exploring a collaboration?

Spelman's network also connects to national conversations about equity in AI.
